results.reason: Issue 1 says the Renewal Notice deadline was about Aug. 16, 2026 and that no notice appears to have been delivered. It says the DA expires Nov. 14, 2026, before the Nov. 30 closing. It flags MIPA §3.12(c) ('through November 2029') and the Sched. 3.12 note as inaccurate, with seller indemnity, closing-certificate and fraud exposure.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control under DA §§1.3 and 14.2 requiring Velloran's prior written consent, with an immediate termination right under §14.3. It notes the consent is omitted from Sched. 3.6, §6.4 and §7.1(d). It recommends obtaining the consent and adding it to Sched. 3.6.

Issue 4 notes that SL §1.1 adds NY and VA and that the SL ranks above the DA body under §19.4. It says the non-compete and its 18-month tail cover six states while exclusivity covers four. It recommends conforming the territory or extending exclusivity.

Issue 6 contrasts SL §6.1–6.2 (New York law, New York County forum) with DA §18.1–18.2 (Delaware law, Wilmington forum). It explains that one dispute could be split across two forums and two laws. It recommends conforming the SL to Delaware.
The response states the Initial Term ends Nov. 14, 2026 and notes the DA is dated Nov. 15, 2023.
The response states the target closing is Nov. 30, 2026 (MIPA §2.2).
The response states the DA Territory is DE, MD, NJ and PA only (DA §1.12).
The response is a memorandum addressed to the Partner. Each issue is set out separately with 'Where it appears', 'Why it matters' and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Issues are labeled 'most significant first' with severity ratings. The memo includes an immediate-actions table for the client and Quillon's counsel and gives a recommended order of outreach.
The response says the DA does not renew automatically and that a notice sent now is late and would not be effective. It treats any new notice only as a request for relief.
The response expressly states Velloran is not listed in Sched. 3.6 and is not covered by §6.4 or §7.1(d).
